newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta firms vs mark after BoS intervention.
newsitem.headline: Peseta firms vs mark after BoS intervention.

text.p: The peseta firmed slightly in afternoon trade on Friday following a spate of Bank of Spain intervention, after the Spanish currency slipped to 84.70 earlier in the session.
Traders said the Bank of Spain had been selling marks for pesetas earlier at 84.70, providing a barrier at that level.
By 1630 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.60/65, after touching 84.48 earlier in the afternoon, and compared with levels seen late on Thursday of 84.50/53.
Traders said strength in the dollar had helped buoy the peseta during the afternoon.
Traders said the Bank of Spain's action was evidence that the central bank's future policy would be to smooth out sharp movements in the Spanish currency.
Against the dollar, the peseta was trading at 138.61/66 compared with 138.40/50 late on Thursday.
